comment: The product record: who this Prism is for, how each of them sees it, and the words it uses with each. After afflom/me's product record (ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010 stakeholders, concerns and viewpoints). Its routing, which decision answers which stakeholder's question, is the proved app prism/apps/stakeholder-view.prompt.json; which front end feature each view shows is the proved app prism/apps/frontend-feature.prompt.json, and which backend capability serves it is prism/apps/backend-capability.prompt.json; this file keeps the words: the persona, the lexicon, each view's question and frame, and journeys made of the apps' own checked examples. Only Prism is implemented in this repository, so the pages that render these words are generated outside it.

brand.name: Platform Prism
brand.tagline: Every platform decision, proved before it ships.
brand.summary: A white-label Prism for teams that run content-addressed platforms: registries, VM images, air-gapped sites and the rollouts that depend on them. Each decision the platform makes is a small app whose rules are proved in Lean, compiled to one verified artifact, and run in your browser.

persona.title: The platform engineer who builds the cloud others stand on
persona.source: Read from public work: GitHub usrbinkat, ContainerCraft (Kargo, Konductor, kmi), UOR-Foundation/kappa-distribution and conference talks. LinkedIn could not be read.
domain: Kubernetes platforms from homelab to regulated and air-gapped sites (Talos, KubeVirt, Cilium, Ceph)
OCI distribution: registries, signed multi-arch VM images, content-addressed storage
Infrastructure as code and reproducible environments (Pulumi, Nix, devcontainers)
Conformance suites that tell the truth (kappa-conformance, OCI distribution-spec parity)
jobs: Know a registry really speaks the protocol before teams depend on it
Never trust an address the spec does not admit
Move images and disks between sites without half-stored uploads
Reclaim storage without losing anything still needed
Run only signed, matching VM images, even with no internet
Give leadership one word, go, hold or no-go, with its reason

viewpoints.title: Platform engineering
viewpoints.question: Can my teams build on this registry, and on these addresses?
viewpoints.frame: You already trust digests: an image pulled by @sha256 is the image you tested. Prism takes the same idea one level up. The decisions your platform makes about those digests are themselves content-addressed apps, and their rules are proved, not just tested.

journey.says: Warnings only: the registry is conformant and CI stays green.
Two MUST failures: nonconformant, exit code 1.
A sha512 label with 64 digits is refused: sha512 needs 128.
An engineer sees the rule that fired and the spec line it cites.

persona.name: Platform engineer
persona.context: Runs the internal developer platform; teams build on the registry she chooses.

jobs: When I adopt a registry, I want one honest conformance verdict, so I can promise teams it speaks kappa-distribution.
When a label arrives from outside, I want to know it is well formed, so the platform never trusts an address the spec does not admit.

viewpoints.title: Cloud engineering
viewpoints.question: Will my images and disks arrive whole, here and at the disconnected site?
viewpoints.frame: Moving VM disks and images between clouds and sites is a chain of uploads and pulls. Prism models each step as a state machine or a policy, so an upload is always committed, rejected or abandoned, and an image is admitted the same way on every cluster.

journey.says: A chunk at the wrong offset changes nothing: resume from the server's range.
The bytes do not hash to the label: rejected with 409, nothing half-stored.

journey.request: verified match arm64 upstream connected ok
journey.says: A signed, matching arm64 image from upstream runs on a connected cluster.
At the disconnected site the proof is read from the sources shipped with the page: nothing reaches the network.

persona.name: Cloud engineer
persona.context: Moves images and VM disks between clouds and a disconnected site.

jobs: When I move an image to a disconnected site, I want it admitted the same way as at home, so nothing behaves differently in the field.
When an upload breaks off, I want to know what state it is in, so I resume instead of starting over.

primary.request: verified match amd64 mirror airgapped ok
primary.lead: Will this image be admitted at the site?

viewpoints.title: Operations and SRE
viewpoints.question: What does the registry keep, and what can I safely reclaim tonight?
viewpoints.frame: Garbage collection is where storage bills and data loss meet. The eviction rule here is the one the spec states, and two of its promises are proved for every blob: an outstanding finalizer and a bound tag always keep a blob.

journey.says: Untagged with an expired pin: the sweep reclaims it.
A finalizer is outstanding: kept until its controller releases it.
A session that went quiet is abandoned and its pin released.

persona.name: Registry operator
persona.context: Keeps the registry healthy and its storage bill sane.

jobs: When storage fills up, I want to know exactly which blobs are safe to reclaim, so I never delete something still needed.
When uploads stall, I want them to expire cleanly, so pins do not leak.

primary.lead: Can this blob be reclaimed tonight?

viewpoints.title: Security and supply chain
viewpoints.question: Can anything unsigned, tampered or from the wrong place ever run?
viewpoints.frame: Supply-chain controls usually live in prose and in tests that sample a few cases. Here each control is a property the Lean kernel proves for every request, and the threat model that names it is generated from the same source.

journey.request: missing match amd64 mirror connected ok
journey.says: No signature: denied.

journey.request: verified match amd64 upstream airgapped ok
journey.says: An air-gapped cluster never runs an upstream pull: denied.

journey.request: verified match amd64 mirror connected error
journey.says: The verifier failed: indeterminate, and nothing runs.
Every answer is computed by the verified guest in the browser, never by a server.

persona.name: Security engineer
persona.context: Owns supply-chain integrity for every workload the platform runs.

jobs: When an image is about to run, I want proof it is signed, intact and from an allowed source, so nothing tampered ever runs.
When the verifier fails, I want the platform to fail closed, so an outage is never a bypass.

primary.request: missing match amd64 mirror connected ok

viewpoints.title: Engineering leadership
viewpoints.question: Are we ready to roll out? Go, hold or no-go.
viewpoints.frame: You need one word and the reason for it. The rollout gate combines the other decisions: is the registry conformant, is its identity key backed up, is the data backed up, is the build reproducible, were the images admitted. It never says go when the key or a backup is missing, and that is proved, not promised.

journey.says: Everything checks out: go.
Nothing is broken, but nothing is proven: hold.
The signing key is not backed up: no-go.
A leader is never handed protocol rules: the rule trace is not shown.

persona.name: Engineering leader
persona.context: Decides whether a platform change ships this week.

jobs: When a rollout is proposed, I want one word with its reason, so I can decide without reading protocol detail.

viewpoints.title: Business and risk
viewpoints.question: What are we paying for, and what could we lose?
viewpoints.frame: Two costs matter: storage you keep and do not need, and data you lose and did need. This Prism keeps both visible. Storage is reclaimed only when nothing still needs it, and a rollout never goes ahead without a complete backup.

journey.says: Nothing holds this blob any more: its storage is reclaimed.
Only part of the data is backed up: hold until it all is.
journey.stage: A partial backup holds the rollout

journey.says: Every UOR word is shown beside its platform word and its plain words.

persona.name: Business owner
persona.context: Pays for the platform and answers for what it could lose.

jobs: When I review the platform's cost, I want to see what storage we keep and why, so we pay only for what is needed.
When a rollout is planned, I want to know nothing can be lost, so the risk is one I can accept.

design.comment: One design system for every view. The builder writes these tokens as CSS custom properties and uses only the components named here.

rules: Text contrast at least 4.5:1, large text 3:1, in light and dark
Every control reachable and operable by keyboard, with a visible focus ring
State is never shown by colour alone: every verdict is a word
Motion is decorative and stops under prefers-reduced-motion
Targets at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels

components.name: AnswerHero
components.purpose: The view's main question, answered first: the verdict as a word, one sentence why, and the few inputs that change it.

components.name: JourneyMap
components.purpose: The stakeholder's journey as ordered stages, each with the stakeholder's goal and the checked answer at that stage.

components.name: DecisionPanel
components.purpose: One decision with every input as a labelled choice; the answer and its reason, with the rule and the proof behind a disclosure.

components.name: Disclosure
components.purpose: Detail one click away: rules, proofs, words and how the view is served.

components.name: Seal
components.purpose: Whether the guest verified and how many acceptance vectors it replayed, always visible.

disclosure.summary: shown as a one-line summary that opens in place
